The list

State of play

What the exam looks like right now

Structure has been stable since December 2018: Paper I is 50 questions for 100 marks, Paper II is 100 questions for 200 marks, both in a single three-hour sitting with no break. Two marks per correct answer and no negative marking, which has one blunt consequence: leaving a question blank is strictly worse than guessing. Attempt all 100.

Recent sessions: the December 2025 English paper was held on 5 January 2026, with the final answer key and result on 4 February 2026. The June 2026 English paper, held 22 June 2026, was cancelled and re-conducted on 9 September 2026 after an expert committee found factual, spelling and translation errors plus heavy repetition of old questions. Treat any circulating "June 2026 English" paper as void.

English cutoffs out of 300, from the official NTA tables: December 2025 gave Unreserved JRF 186, Assistant Professor 164, PhD-only 146. June 2025 gave Unreserved JRF 188, Assistant Professor 166. A widely shared "212" figure for June 2025 is a coaching estimate, not NTA's number.

Format

Roughly half the paper is not single-fact recall

Since 2019 four formats dominate. Approximate shares, from coaching breakdowns rather than published NTA statistics, so treat them as direction not gospel:

  • Match List I with List II — consistently the largest single format, around a fifth to a quarter of the paper.
  • Multi-statement combination (five statements A to E, choose which are correct) — the fastest-growing format across 2024 to 2026.
  • Chronological sequencing — several per paper, often mixing works by one author or quotations across three centuries.
  • Assertion and Reason — present but volatile. Prominent in December 2025, reportedly absent from the voided June 2026 paper.
  • Comprehension — two passages, roughly ten questions, inference-weighted rather than fact-retrieval.

The implication for how you study is unglamorous: single-fact flashcard recall trains you for the minority of the paper. All four dominant formats require holding four to five items in working memory at once and permuting them. That is a different skill and it needs its own drilling.

Unit weighting, December 2025

British Literature 27, Literary Theory 15, Literary Criticism 11, Indian Writing 10, Comprehension 10, Cultural Studies 9, Language and Linguistics 9, Literary Research 5, American and World 4. British Literature plus Theory plus Criticism is over half the paper.

Repeat offenders

Who keeps showing up

Every paper, without exception: Shakespeare. Near-certain: Chaucer, Milton, T. S. Eliot, Virginia Woolf. Frequent: Beckett, Yeats, Hardy, Dickens, Forster, Pinter, R. K. Narayan, Toni Morrison, Edward Said.

Theory names with near-automatic term mapping, worth memorising as pairs because the paper tests exactly this link: subaltern to Spivak, binary opposition to Saussure and Lévi-Strauss, interpellation to Althusser, hybridity and mimicry and third space to Bhabha, objective correlative to Eliot, chronotope and dialogism and carnivalesque to Bakhtin, structure of feeling to Raymond Williams, encoding and decoding to Stuart Hall, bricolage to Lévi-Strauss, panopticon to Bentham by way of Foucault.

Recurring term-and-genre tests: closet drama, dub poetry, bucolic, confessional, topographical, kenning, metonymy versus synecdoche, Bildungsroman versus Künstlerroman versus Erziehungsroman.

Distractor design

Six ways this paper tries to fool you

1 — The sibling work

All four options are genuinely by the named author. Only one belongs to the specific grouping asked about. Dec 2025: which is NOT in Beckett's trilogy? Molloy, Murphy, Malone Dies, The Unnamable. Murphy is Beckett's, just not part of the trilogy.

2 — The one-word swap inside a true sentence

A long, plausible statement with a single altered noun. Read the nouns, not the rhythm. Dec 2025: "English and French culture in Where Angels Fear to Tread." Everything is right except the nationality. It is Italian.

3 — The name inside the quotation

The quoted passage mentions a writer, and that writer appears as an option. It is almost never the answer. June 2025: "Shakespeare was the Homer... Jonson was the Virgil." Ben Jonson is an option. The answer is Dryden.

4 — The famous populariser versus the actual originator

You meet a concept through one thinker but it was coined by another. Panopticon: Bentham designed it, Foucault analysed it. "What Is an Author?" is Foucault, 1969; "The Death of the Author" is Barthes, 1967. Two years and two writers apart.

5 — The near-miss date in sequencing

Two items sit within three or four years of each other, and the four options differ only in whether those two are swapped. Do not try to date all five. Fix the earliest and the latest, and check which option honours both.

6 — The absolute in a multi-statement set

In A-to-E combination questions, the false statements usually announce themselves with only, always, never, merely or permanent. Theory rarely says anything that flatly. "Dalit writing is only a political category" and "strategic essentialism is a permanent programme" are both wrong for the same structural reason.

Guessing, done properly

Four moves that convert a blank into a coin-flip you win

  • Anchor and eliminate, for match-the-list. Find the one pairing you are certain of and strike out every option that contradicts it. You will usually be down to two, and a second known pair finishes it. You almost never need all four pairings, so do not read all four before starting.
  • Scan for the intruder, for "which set consists entirely of". Do not verify every item. Look for the one that does not belong. A Yeats list with "Fern Hill" in it is out on sight.
  • Extremes first, for chronology. Identify the oldest and the newest item. Most option sets can be killed on the first or last position alone.
  • Count the statements, for combination questions. If three options include statement (A) and one does not, (A) is probably correct and the real decision is elsewhere. Option overlap leaks information about which statements the examiner considers true.

And the structural point that beats all four: with no negative marking, an eliminated-down-to-two guess is worth an expected one mark. Across fifteen such questions that is fifteen marks, which is the distance between the Assistant Professor and JRF cutoffs in most recent English cycles.

Sourcing

How reliable is what you are drilling

Questions carry a badge where relevant. PYQ 25/26 means a December 2025 or June 2025 item reconstructed from coaching sources and independently fact-checked before inclusion; the answer is verified, the exact wording may differ from the original. Written means I wrote it to cover a syllabus gap or drill a format. Everything unbadged came from your two solved-paper PDFs.

Comprehension questions now carry their own sub-categories: Detail and Reference, Inference, Vocabulary in Context, Poetry Extract, Tone and Style, Main Idea and Title. Where the original passage could be recovered from the PDF it is shown above the question; 212 questions now carry theirs. The 184 whose passage could not be recovered sit in their own category, Passage missing (answer unaided), switched off in a mixed session but one click away when you want them. They keep their real topic in the question header, so you can still see whether a miss was a poetry extract or a prose argument.

Answer keys have been audited. Where an explanation names its own answer, that claim was compared against the stored key: 1,840 keys agree and carry a green key checked badge. Three keys were corrected where the evidence favoured the explanation, nine questions were removed where key and explanation could not be reconciled, and twenty-five were removed as structurally damaged. 381 explanations had the next question's text bleeding into them from the PDF's second column; that bleed has been trimmed. The rest carry key unchecked, meaning the source stated the answer only once so there was nothing to check it against. You can restrict a session to cross-checked keys from the setup screen.

Only NTA's own answer keys are authoritative. Where a reconstruction disagreed with established fact, the question was left out rather than guessed at.
